// diagnostic

E1110

The bare `task` keyword needs a lexical `task.group` or a `Group` parameter, always targets the innermost active one, or `Group` is stored or captured by an escaping lambda.

What

The bare `task` keyword needs a lexical `task.group` or a `Group` parameter, always targets the innermost active one, or `Group` is stored or captured by an escaping lambda.

Why

Structured spawning uses the innermost active lexical `task.group` or a direct `Group` parameter. A group may flow down the call stack, but it cannot become stored state or escape its scope.

Fix

Write `task work()` inside the active group, or pass that handle directly to `fn helper(group: Group)`; do not store or capture it.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E1110: tests/ui/taskgroup_parameter_aggregate.stderr.

Error [E1110]: `Group` cannot be stored inside another value
  --> tests/ui/taskgroup_parameter_aggregate.jet:2:5
    |
  2 |     groups :: [group]
    |     ^^^^^^
 Why: a task group is call-stack-only spawn authority; aliases and aggregates could outlive its owner
 Fix: pass `group: Group` directly to a helper function or method and use it there
